thread_analysis.thread_summary: Short internal Allion thread (Alps Alpine) about uFL-to-SMA cable incompatibility discovered when the DUT arrived for an RF PHY test. Sakai had warned the customer's contact in advance that the lab's uFL-to-SMA cables might not mate with the DUT's connector and asked them to be ready to supply their own, but the customer never confirmed and simply shipped the DUT. None of Allion's lab cables/adapters fit. A second, related issue arose during setup: a new test engineer found the DUT had two candidate antenna terminals (one shown in the customer's antenna spec document, requiring the top cover to be removed; one on an externally exposed circuit board) and needed guidance on which to use. Sakai directed staff to use the externally accessible terminal and to ask the customer to ship their own SMA conversion cable.
all_questions_found: None of the lab's uFL-to-SMA cables/adapters fit the DUT's connector — does the DUT need modification, or should the customer supply a cable? (-> case_01)
The DUT has two possible antenna connection points (one behind the top cover, one on an externally exposed board) — which one should the RF test connect to? (-> case_02)
Should we ask the customer to send their own SMA conversion cable since none of ours fit? (-> case_01)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: uFL (u.FL) micro RF connectors are not fully standardized across manufacturers. Physical dimensions may be similar but electrical contact and mechanical mating reliability vary between manufacturers. In this case the incompatibility was not just a theoretical risk — it was confirmed at the lab, despite Allion having multiple uFL-to-SMA cables and adapters on hand from past purchases. Separately, ambiguity about which of two physical antenna terminals to use (one requiring DUT disassembly, one externally accessible) required an internal engineering judgment call, resolved in favor of the non-invasive terminal.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: RF measurement accuracy depends on a proper RF signal path. Any physical connector mismatch at the DUT-to-cable interface introduces measurement error or complete signal loss, making test results invalid. When no available cable fits, the correct response is to request a customer-supplied cable rather than assume DUT modification is needed. When multiple physical antenna terminals exist, prefer the externally accessible (non-disassembly) terminal absent contrary technical reason.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Discovering uFL connector incompatibility during the RF test session means the test cannot proceed until a compatible cable is sourced from the customer, adding delay. Connecting to the wrong antenna terminal, or unnecessarily disassembling the DUT, risks invalid measurements or DUT damage.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The pre-shipment heads-up about possible cable incompatibility was left as an open offer ('let us know if it doesn't fit') rather than a firm instruction, and the customer's silence was not followed up on before the DUT was shipped — this could have been caught before the DUT was even sent, avoiding the lab-side delay.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Add a standard pre-test checklist item for RF test sessions involving modules with uFL connectors: (1) confirm connector manufacturer and part number with the customer in advance; (2) explicitly request the customer ship their own uFL-to-SMA cable rather than leaving it as an optional ask; (3) follow up if the customer does not respond before shipping the DUT; (4) when a DUT has multiple candidate antenna terminals, confirm with the customer or experienced staff which is correct before connecting, preferring non-invasive (externally accessible) terminals.
